newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ansett says cleared for daily Osaka flights.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ansett says cleared for daily Osaka flights.

text.p: Australia's fledgling international airline, Ansett, has won approval to run daily flights between Osaka in Japan and Australia from mid-year.
The Canberra-based International Air Services Commission confirmed on Tuesday it had allocated extra capacity to Ansett along the busy tourism corridor.

Ansett, equally owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd, said the go-ahead fulfilled a strategic and commercial objective to offer daily flights to Japanese travellers, who comprise Australia's biggest tourism market.

"Japan is Australia's major in-bound tourism market and economic sustainability of any airline route in any major market is heavily influenced by being, at minimum, able to operate on a daily basis," Ansett spokesman Peter Young told Reuters.

Ansett runs five flights per week out of Osaka using Boeing 747s. It will run an additional two flights per week using Boeing 767s from around June and will upgrade this in November to a daily Boeing 747 service, Young said.
Ansett also wants to run daily flights between Hong Kong and Australian ports, calling this another key strategic objective.
The airline flies five days a week out of Hong Kong and extra capacity along this route has yet to be agreed between Australian and Hong Kong authorities, Young said.
